Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players have already made their way out to the middle. Sarah Forbes and Gaby Lewis are the two openers for Ireland Women. Titas Sadhu to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

When you concede over 400 runs, there’s little to highlight about the bowling performance. Sloppy fielding, missed catches, and far too many extras only added to Ireland’s woes. While the pitch heavily favored the batters, the Irish bowlers struggled to find consistent lines and lengths, making life easier for the opposition. Despite the challenges, Orla Prendergast managed to grab a couple of wickets, while Arlene Kelly, Freya Sargent, and Georgina Dempsey picked up one each. The only silver lining was their slight recovery in the death overs. Now, their batters face an uphill battle to even come close to this daunting target. Stay tuned as we bring you the second chapter!

The player of the moment, Pratika Rawal is up for a quick chat. She says that she was going ball by ball and was not thinking much about how many runs to score. Adds that she was a bit slow after getting to the 70s and needs to work on that, but she covered up well after reaching the hundred. Mentions that it is a treat to watch Smriti Mandhana bat and she likes to take a backseat when Smriti hits them out of the park. Says that they wanted to cross 400 and are happy that they touched 430 in the end. Further adds that there is no magic and she and Smriti are very comfortable with each other; they don't think about records and play the ball on its merit, which makes the difference.

India Women thought Smriti Mandhana’s wicket would bring relief, but what followed was pure carnage! Richa Ghosh, promoted up the order, unleashed a flurry of strokes, while young Pratika Rawal stole the spotlight with a sensational maiden ODI century. Rawal’s blistering 154 off 129 balls was a masterclass of poise and power, taking India Women to the brink of 400. Tejal Hasabnis and Harleen Deol, along with a few others added the finishing touches, ensuring a historic total that left fans in absolute awe!

India Women, led by a fiery Smriti Mandhana and Pratika Rawal, put on a batting masterclass after opting to bat on a belter of a pitch. The openers unleashed carnage, smashing 90 runs in the Powerplay - the highest of the series and notched their fourth 100-run stand in the last six innings. Skipper Mandhana was unstoppable, blasting the fastest ODI century for India Women in just 70 balls, and her 135 off 80 balls included a record-breaking seven sixes. The pair added a staggering 233-run partnership, rewriting records and leaving the Irish bowlers in tatters.

INDIA WOMEN MAKE HISTORY! They've recorded their highest-ever ODI total, becoming just the third team after Australia Women and New Zealand Women to surpass the 400-run milestone. It was a breathtaking batting performance from the hosts. While Smriti Mandhana dazzled with the fastest ODI century for India Women, it was the young sensation Pratika Rawal who stole the show with a remarkable 154.

Skipper Gaby Lewis has led from the front, while Christina Coulter Reilly and Leah Paul have also contributed valuable runs. However, the rest of the batting lineup needs to step up and deliver. On the bowling front, they struggled in the previous game and will be aiming for a stronger comeback, with Orla Prendergast, Ava Canning, and Arlene Kelly  playing key roles. Can the Irish pull off an upset, or will the hosts seal the series with a clean sweep? Stay tuned to find out - toss and team news coming up shortly!

In Harmanpreet Kaur’s absence, Smriti Mandhana has taken the reins with confidence, while rising stars Pratika Rawal and Tejal Hasabnis have stolen the spotlight with their performances. The batting lineup is firing on all cylinders, with Jemimah Rodrigues dazzling the crowd with a stunning century in their record-breaking total last game. However, with the series already sealed, we can expect a few changes in the side. Priya Mishra and Deepti Sharma have spun webs around the Irish batters, and Titas Sadhu along with Sayali Satghare will be eager to leave their mark in this final showdown.

We are down to the final act of the ODI series between India Women and Ireland Women at the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot. Coming into this series, India were the clear favourites, even with a couple of seniors rested and some fresh faces in the squad. The hosts have lived up to the billing, sealing the series 2-0 with dominant performances. In the second ODI, Jemimah Rodrigues stole the spotlight with her maiden ODI century, propelling India to 370, their highest in women’s ODI cricket, surpassing their previous best of 358. The victory was never in doubt after such a commanding display, but for the second consecutive game, the visitors showed resilience by batting out their 50 overs. Ireland’s batting performances have been commendable throughout the series. Before this series, their highest ODI total against India was 169, but they surpassed it twice, posting 238 in the first ODI and 254 in the second. Christina Coulter Reilly, Leah Paul, and captain Gaby Lewis have been standout performers with the bat, offering positives for Ireland to build on going into the ODI World Cup Qualifier. However, while the pitches in Rajkot have been far from bowler-friendly, Lewis and her team would acknowledge they could have delivered better with the ball and, more critically, in the field. Ground fielding and catching have been areas of concern, which they must address moving forward. Speaking of fielding, it remains a weak link for India too. Despite the dominance, their struggles in ground fielding and catching persist, an issue they must rectify ahead of the ODI World Cup later this year. The hosts retained the same XI for the second ODI, but with the series in the bag, they are likely to make changes for this final encounter. Uma Chetry, Raghvi Bist, Minnu Mani, and Tanuja Kanwer are yet to feature in the series. With the next ODI series scheduled for July in England, this match provides an ideal opportunity for India to test different combinations and fine-tune their plans for the future. Can the Irish conjure a collective display, provide a stiffer challenge, and who knows, even pull off a surprise? We shall find out soon enough.
